title: 2026 Global M&A Outlook
summary: A global survey-based outlook on M&A, moving from a retrospective of 2025 to 2026 dealmaking themes and implications. Its main topics include strategic focus, differences between buyer types, portfolio simplification, AI-enabled deal execution, execution discipline, and industry-specific dynamics. The research surveyed 700 dealmakers across 20 countries and jurisdictions.

sections.title: About the research
sections.summary: Describes the survey behind the report, including its respondent base, coverage, and fieldwork period.
key_points: The survey included 700 M&A dealmakers across 20 countries and jurisdictions and was fielded from 19 December 2025 to 27 January 2026.
Respondents comprised 519 corporate dealmakers and 181 respondents from private equity firms; they were senior executives involved in M&A decision-making across 10 sectors.

sections.title: AI-driven transformation of deal execution
sections.summary: Discusses how AI can expand and change deal-execution analysis, including diligence and integration monitoring. The report argues that AI can make previously uneconomical analyses viable, while people retain review and decision authority.
key_points: AI-enabled analysis can make new categories of work worthwhile, rather than only speeding up existing analysis.
Examples include clause-by-clause contract comparison and continuous monitoring of separation dependencies, TSA milestones, and performance indicators.
An AI agent can model customer concentration risk, compare it with benchmarks, draft diligence material, and flag anomalies; the human reviews and decides while the agent executes.

sections.title: Execution discipline as a decisive source of advantage
sections.summary: Focuses on integration planning and execution as determinants of deal outcomes. The report emphasizes that outcomes are shaped early by planning, sequencing, and governance rather than by post-close heroics.
key_points: The section emphasizes readiness before close and argues that integration outcomes are shaped early.
Identified integration priorities include synergy realization, integration due diligence, and integrating cultures, processes, and systems.
